lessonRef.title: Explicit model: comparing two pretend prices

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 3 — spending and comparing
objective: Learners compare two invented prices for the same item, find the difference, and scale the saving across several units to see that a small gap repeats.
scenario: Lena is an invented third grader comparing two pretend stores for the same pack of pencils. The made-up Corner Store charges $2.40 a pack and the made-up Market Stand charges $2.15 a pack. The packs and the stores are both imaginary.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Look at Lena's two pretend prices for the identical pencil pack.

prompts.text: What is the lower of Lena's two pretend prices?

tasks.directions: Find how far apart Lena's two stores are on the same pack, then say plainly which store is the cheaper one.

prompts.text: How much less is the Market Stand pack than the Corner Store pack?
Which pretend store sells the pencil pack for less?

tasks.directions: Lena's pretend class needs 3 identical packs, and every pack costs the same at each store.

prompts.text: What do 3 packs cost at the Market Stand?
How much less is that than 3 packs at the Corner Store?

tasks.directions: The gap on one pack was small; the gap on three was not.

prompts.text: Why is comparing prices worth Lena's time even when the difference on one pack looks tiny?

remediation: If a learner compares the totals by re-adding both stores from scratch and loses track, have them find the one-pack gap first and add that same gap three times, so the repeated structure is visible rather than buried in two long sums.
extension: Ask the learner how many packs Lena would have to buy before the saving passes $1.00, and to justify the count.
